title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of chub mackerel (Scomber japonicus) from the Indo-Pacific Ocean
abstract: Chub mackerels (Scomber japonicus) are a migratory marine fish widely distributed in the Indo-Pacific Ocean. They are globally consumed for their high Omega-3 content, but their population is declining due to global warming. Here, we generated the first chromosome-level genome assembly of chub mackerel (fScoJap1) using the Vertebrate Genomes Project assembly pipeline with PacBio HiFi genomic sequencing and Arima Hi-C chromosome contact data. The final assembly is 828.68 Mb with 24 chromosomes, nearly all containing telomeric repeats at their ends. We annotated 31,656 genes and discovered that approximately 2.19% of the genome contained DNA transposon elements repressed within duplicated genes. Analyzing 5-methylcytosine (5mC) modifications using HiFi reads, we observed open/close chromatin patterns at gene promoters, including the FADS2 gene involved in Omega-3 production. This chromosome-level reference genome provides unprecedented opportunities for advancing our knowledge of chub mackerels in biology, industry, and conservation.

narrative:
Short impact summary

This 2023 Scientific Data article is an open-access foundational genome resource for chub mackerel, a widely distributed Indo-Pacific fish of ecological and fishery interest. Its impact is still early but visible: the record shows 3 citations and 4 documented downstream reuse signals, alongside use in follow-on chub mackerel studies and related vertebrate genomics work.

Full narrative

The article’s main contribution is methodological and infrastructural. It reports the first chromosome-level genome assembly of chub mackerel, generated with the Vertebrate Genomes Project pipeline using PacBio HiFi sequencing and Arima Hi-C data. That makes the work a reference point for subsequent genetics and functional studies on Scomber japonicus, especially where high-quality genome structure is needed for marker discovery, candidate-gene analysis, and comparative genomics.

The uptake record supports that role. OpenAlex currently shows 3 citations, which is an early signal rather than a mature citation history, but the citing landscape is already thematically coherent. Later papers use the assembly in chub mackerel-focused genomics and immunology research, including work on sex-associated markers, off-target assessment after genome editing, and functional studies of genes involved in apoptosis, oxidative stress, and immune modulation. This pattern suggests the assembly is being used as enabling infrastructure rather than cited as a standalone object.

Reuse signals reinforce that interpretation. The digest records 4 downstream reuse instances, including article and preprint reuse, and a Europe PMC article mention. The work also appears in scholarly contexts tied to genomics, chromatin, methylation, and aquaculture disease management, indicating that its relevance extends beyond one narrow application area. Because the source record is still sparse, the safest reading is that the paper has begun to seed a small but concrete research network around chub mackerel genomics.

The stewardship profile is also notable. The article is open access and linked to supporting code or data repositories, which improves retrievability and reuse. Funding from the National Research Foundation of Korea, the Korea Institute of Marine Science and Technology promotion, Howard Hughes Medical Institute, and the Wellcome Trust points to a cross-institutional, internationally supported genomics effort. In short, this is a resource paper whose value lies in creating a durable genomic reference that is already being carried forward into subsequent biological and aquaculture research.
